steps.content: Life in the Bureau runs like a train on its predetermined tracks. Most days are regular and uneventful.
After doing her confinement time, Dove returns to her room and resumes her normal life. No one approaches her about the incident again or demands she face any additional consequences.

Chief's special attention also fades away with those consequences. In the bustling Bureau, that day's events were nothing more than sparks ignited on the tracks when a train rounds a bend, deserving no one's special notice.
The pages of her life don't cease turning. She follows a routine, reads books she never had access to before, and occasionally, when the mood strikes her...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Oh, don't sigh like that. I read that it may drive good luck away. If something's bothering you... I'm all ears. Don't worry, it'll be our little secret!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: You can't tell that Sinner you admire her because you're staff... Why not try writing a letter? You don't have to put your name in it. If your feelings are sincere, it'll surely move her!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Would you like me to deliver your letter? It's no trouble at all. No, thank you for trusting me! Just wait here, I'll make sure to bring back a reply...
Dove waves goodbye with a smile, her skirt billowing as she turns the corner. But instead of going to her supposed destination, she heads straight to her own room.
The moment the door closes, she instantly wipes the smile from her face and casually tosses the letter onto her desk.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: It's just another boring letter, but I suppose it's better than nothing. Now, how should I respond to this admiration in the idol's voice...
She smooths out the paper and envelope with practiced ease, taps the pen against her lips for a moment pensively, then, having made up her mind, slowly lowers the nib...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: You're nothing but a cowardly, greedy cockroach obsessed with forgery. You make me sick just looking at you!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Messengers... are people who deliver emotions and connect souls. Any one of them is a hundred times more noble than you!
A drop of ink drips from her idle pen, blooming into a dark stain on the blank paper. The sudden invasion of memories grips her wrist like a vice, making it impossible for her to start writing.
...It happens again. After struggling briefly, Dove lets out a resigned sigh, puts down her pen, and crumples the ink-stained paper before tossing it into the corner.
Though Dove has been trying her hardest to avoid remembering that day, she knows she can't run away from these memories.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I thought you said idealism was dead and pointless.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If that's the case... why did you get so worked up? Where did this rage come from?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Yeah, why? Why don't you tell me? Why should I know?

She seems to be speaking both to someone in her memories and to herself. The question that has been haunting her all this time resurfaces, tearing her between conflicting thoughts until she's left completely at a loss.

steps.speaker: Staff Member
steps.content: Really? You'll do that? Thank you! Thank you so much! I had no idea being a mail carrier was such a noble profession... You've really helped me out of a tough spot!

steps.speaker: Staff Member
steps.content: I don't think this job exists in DisCity anymore. Isn't it some kind of ancient occupation? Oh, sorry, I must sound really ignorant... I'll make sure to learn more about it!

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: A noble... profession...
Perhaps the letters she always carries with her are guiding her, or perhaps the girl's gratitude has stirred something deep within her heart.
By the time Dove snaps out of it, she's already cleared away the envelopes and paper meant for forged letters, leaving only fresh blank sheets waiting silently on her desk.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Could this be... an answer?

The girl stares down at the blank paper that seems to be both guiding and questioning her, hesitating for a long while. Slowly, the intermittent scratching of her pen breaks the silence as more and more crumpled drafts gather at her feet.
After countless revisions, the neat and firm writing finally appears on the envelope...

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: "To Mom and Dad"
She draws in a deep breath and, mustering her courage, picks up her pen.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: You'll never guess where I'm writing this letter—DisCity. But it's really not that fancy of a place. There's this Bureau here, and their Chief is kind of a control freak who can be mean to me sometimes, calling me a liar.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: Although... fine, that's the truth! But did he have to point it out right to my face? Even if he's always right about everything, that's not very nice!
steps.female_content: Although... fine, that's the truth! But did she have to point it out right to my face? Even if she's always right about everything, that's just not fair!

steps.content: Contrary to her usual efficiency in forging others' letters, Dove is taking her time with her own letter. She opens up her heart hesitantly, carefully choosing each word as she reveals the true feelings she's kept hidden for so long.
Her words are neither diplomatic nor mature. In fact, they're simply a sulking child's complaints meant only for her parents.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: To be honest, back in Désir, I really got a thrill out of deceiving people. It made me feel so superior and powerful. I even wanted to keep doing it forever.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: A mere letter could make them laugh and cry, stirring up joy and despair... and I was the only one who knew it was all fake! The letters, the smiles, the tears. Everything was just a lie! Haha!
Watching others fall for her deceptions, Dove convinced herself that becoming a deceiver meant she could never fall victim to lies again.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: It wasn't until that person scolded me that I started to realize I was wrong. The truth is, I've been lied to all along too.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: By myself.
She forged letters to take revenge on the villagers in her hometown, because they relied on the mail carriers to bring back messages while carelessly dismissing their sacrifice.

She also used lies to punish the people of Désir, for they never once saw through her deceptions and only proved her bitter, disillusioning assumption repeatedly: No one truly cared about a messenger's idealistic mission.
But in truth, the one she really wanted to get back at might have been someone else entirely.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: I wanted to trick myself. Maybe the DisCity dream was real? Maybe the messenger dream too? Maybe someday someone would tell me our dedication to our job wasn't all in vain, that my mom and dad were worthy of respect.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: Maybe you're just held up somewhere, like it was written in those letters Uncle and Aunt showed me. If I just wait a little longer, you'll come back and tell me this was all just a joke, just a little test to help me grow up faster...

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: But why won't you come back? I've deceived so many people and told so many lies. I've become such a terrible child. Why won't you come back already?
Her parents abandoned her to pursue their career. And with the truth concealed by the villagers' fake letters, she refused to believe that her parents were already dead.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: Shouldn't you be scolding me right now, like you used to? Tell me it's wrong to lie, that it's a crime to forge letters. Tell me a good child should face reality with courage instead of hiding behind lies like a loser.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: But I'll never hear those words again. You're never coming back...
The nib of her pen digs deep into the paper as she scribbles on and on, each word like a liberating cry.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: Mom, Dad, why did you just leave like that... Why did you leave me alone...
She's scribbling so hard that the pen skids off the edge of the paper. The sound of writing filling the room stops abruptly.
She hunches over the desk like a cold plaster statue. Only her trembling fingers gripping the pen reveals the tempest raging within her.

The air seems to freeze, and time becomes a hazy blur. The girl stares at her messy handwriting for what feels like an eternity before finally gripping her pen again, letting the words flow out like a stream.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: I know I was wrong. I understand I've done so many unforgivable things. But I... all I wanted was for you not to suddenly leave me behind.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: Don't choose your noble calling over me. Dove doesn't want to be the thing you throw away.

steps.speaker: Dove's Letter
steps.content: I'll apologize, I'll atone for my actions. So please, just come back to see me one more time. Just once is enough. I just want to say goodbye...
...Even though she knows it's impossible.
Dove sets down her pen and meticulously folds the letter. She takes out an envelope and slips in the paper skillfully, sealing it carefully before finally standing up.
But then she halts at her next move. She stands still as an indescribable disoriented feeling washes over her, making her want to laugh suddenly.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Right... How will I even send this letter? Find a mail carrier? ...But I am the mail carrier.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Nowhere to send it, and no chance of ever getting a reply... Should I end up using my special power on myself, forging replies to fuel my own delusions?
This letter has nowhere to go, just like her who's finally stepped out of her web of lies. There's no place left for her in this imaginary wonderland that's long collapsed.
At that moment, a familiar voice cuts through the loneliness and desolation binding her, reaching out like a helping hand to her lost soul.
Chief's POV

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Dove?
The girl before you seems completely unaware of your presence until now, her eyes going wide with an uncharacteristic startled look.
Not wanting her to feel like you're intruding on her vulnerable moment, you take the initiative to speak first, keeping your tone casual but direct.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't get the wrong idea, I'm just doing my routine patrol and happen to see you heading out. ...Got something to attend to?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Ah... N-nothing.
She nervously tries to hide the letter behind her back, but you didn't come here to let her keep concealing her problems.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't worry, I won't open any letters without permission unless they're going out of the Bureau. There's no need to hide it from me.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Of course you don't need to read the letters, Chief. Not when you have those almighty shackles. What secrets can we Sinners possibly keep when you can just use them on us?
Understanding what your words implied, Dove narrows her eyes and puffs up her cheeks in a pout.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: You already know what I'm trying to do, don't you? So why even bother asking?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because I think that once you've sorted everything out, you'll need someone to confide in. Someone you can be completely honest and open with.
Compared to the Dove who put on an innocent disguise to achieve her goals, her true self might be more difficult to deal with.
But you know this means you're closer to the real her than anyone else has ever been. What you both need now isn't empty pleasantries, but complete honesty.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'd say I'm a pretty good candidate for that role, don't you think? After all, I've been waiting for your answer for quite some time now.
Your straightforward words seem to shatter the invisible wall between you. After a moment of silence, Dove steps aside, opening the door to her room.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Come in.
You follow Dove into her room. Limited by the conditions here, the furnishings look quite different from her room in Désir, yet you can still see echoes of that study in this space.
This time, you sit down by the desk as told by the host. Dove carefully smooths out the creases in the letter before placing it on the desk between you.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: It's all because of your strange questions. These past few days, I haven't been able to sleep or read properly anymore.
She complains, mustering a cheerful tone. You simply listen quietly, waiting for her to ready herself to open up.
You don't have to wait long. Soon, Dove stops fidgeting and looks you in the eye with a seriousness you've never seen in her before.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Chief... No, ${PlayerName}. I want to tell you I'm angry because I can't forgive those people who look down on messengers.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: But deep down, I know the last person I can forgive is myself.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: My parents were gone. My mail carrier dream shattered. I discovered that everything I used to believe in, the letters, the books, even the words themselves... were nothing but elaborate lies...

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: I watched as my world crumbled into a pile of unrecognizable mess I couldn't piece back together. But what did I do as I watched it all happen?
Dove takes a deep breath, trying to steady the tremor in her voice.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...Nothing. I was so afraid of getting hurt again that I couldn't even look at the fragments, much less try to piece them back together.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: All that pessimism and detachment were just concealment for my own weakness. Looking at it now, I'm no different from those who willingly believed my lies, reluctant to face reality.
She lowers her head, gently tracing the recipient's name on the envelope with her fingers, her eyes dim with sorrow.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Even if I understand my mistakes now, even if I want to atone for them... what then? I've already lost everything. I don't even have anyone left to write to.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: For someone like me who's lost hope and faith in everything, if I can't even rely on lies, what meaning could the future possibly hold?
Dove withdraws her hand. You watch as her delicate fingers tremble in the air, hovering uncertainly before finally coming to rest on her lap, where she clasps her hands tightly together.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: I can't say I fully understand what you're going through, but...

choices.text: I can't say I fully understand what you're going through, but...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But have you ever thought... perhaps you could write to me?

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...You?
She looks up at you, her voice feeble and filled with doubt and uncertainty, but you catch a fleeting glimpse of hope in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, but not just me. The Bureau will make a fair judgment about your past crimes, and until you complete your necessary rehabilitation, we'll be here to support you every step of the way.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We'll help you break free from the mire of your past, help you find more people to write to, and let you see for yourself all the things still worth believing in.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Dove, you're no longer that housebound child whose understanding of the world came only from the words others brought back to you. You've seen more now, and you know better what's worth believing in.
You fix your gaze on her wavering eyes and strengthen your tone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rising anew from ruins, sprouting from scorched earth, gaining formidable strength from pain and suffering. This is what it means to be a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Dove, you can do this. Because you've already won once before.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: C-can I really? Delivering emotions, connecting hearts... I've strayed from my dream for so long. I'm afraid I won't be able to stay the course...
The girl mumbles self-deprecating words and shrinks back. You can almost see that sickly child she once was, clutching the doorframe, yearning to step outside yet paralyzed by fear.
Now it's your turn to extend a hand to her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's normal to be afraid, to have doubts, to feel uncertain. Even the most committed idealists cannot be sure they are on the right path from the start.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's no big deal to get lost from time to time, because Dove, I've never seen anyone more devoted to the mail carrier profession than you. I know you can find your way back.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Don't be ridiculous. How many mail carriers can you have met? Besides, I've been on the wrong path for so long...
She protests in a slightly choked voice. This makes you smile, and with gentle words, you take the hand of that child standing by the door, slowly guiding her out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's all right, we've got plenty of time. There's no need to rush.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We'll be right beside you as you find your way back to the beginning, just like when you first learned to read and write, when you first learned to believe in the power of words.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...${PlayerName}...
A teardrop falls onto the envelope, blurring the recipient's name. You know these overwhelming emotions won't subside quickly, so you keep your promise in silence, staying quietly by her side.

These fragments of her dream and faith have been forgotten for too long, but both you and Dove, who has chosen to gather them up again, believe that one day these pieces can be shaped back into her mail carrier dream again.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: ...This letter is for you. I know you're busy and might not have time to write back... but I'll keep waiting.
At long last, Dove regains her composure. She grabs the letter from the desk and presses it into your hands decisively. The letter feels heavy and warm.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I promise I won't keep you waiting for too long.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Oh right, and I've got some good news for you.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Good news?
You smile at her bewildered expression and continue slowly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Remember that merchant whom you met with? I heard that after he was escorted out of the Bureau, he couldn't keep his mouth shut and kept spewing insults about Outlanders.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Somehow he ended up in the immigrant district and got jumped by some guys. They gave him quite the beating.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: Somehow?
You think of Dove's face when she acts innocent and gives your best shot at an impression.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yeah, somehow. You know, these things just happen sometimes.
She watches your hammy performance for a moment before bursting into laughter.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: All right, dear Chief who clearly has nothing to do with that. I'd love it if you could include a story about some crooked merchant and the hero who punished him in your letter.

steps.speaker: Dove
steps.content: In exchange, I can tell you a story... about a frail girl's journey through WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Deal.
You rise with a smile, carefully tucking away her letter. This time, she walks you to the door to see you off, and you both know that a new day is about to begin.
